To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

guanidinoacetic acid, an endogenous metabolite that accumulates in patients with guanidino-acetate methyltransferase deficiency, inhibits complexes II and II-II of the respiratory chain as well as Na(+),K(+) ATPase and creatine-kinase activities in striatum of rat in vivo.

the inhibitory effect of guanidinacetate on the activity of the respiratory chain and on Na(+),K (+)-ATPase can be differentially reversed by taurine administration, while vitamins E and C can reverse the inhibitory effects on CK and Na(+)-K(+)ATPase, and on the oxidative damage.

the effects of GAA administration on the activities of respiratory chain complexes II and II-II, Na(+), K(+)-ATPases and CK can be prevented by taurin and vitamins E and/or C administration in striatum of rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of striatum energy homeostasis in a neurometabolic disease.
the identification of new therapeutic strategies for this disease.
the study of the biochemical and molecular mechanisms underlying striatal damage in GAMT-deficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the in vivo effects of taurine and the antioxidant properties of vitamins E and C can be useful in the therapy of patients with GAMTD, in particular in those patients with a high degree of striatal damage.
the in vivo administration of taurine, vitamin E or vitamin C can be considered as potential therapeutic agents for patients with GAMT deficiency.
GAA is able to cause oxidative stress and to alter the energy metabolism in striatum, and that these effects may be mediated, at least in part, by oxidative damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

GAA administration (intrastriatal) in vivo causes a reduction in the activities of Na(+), K(+)-ATP-ase and CK, as well as in the citric acid cycle activity and the complexes II and II/III of the respiratory chain.
the effects of GAA administration in vivo are not only on the inhibition of Na(+), K(+)-ATPases and CK activities and increase of TBARS, but also on complexes II, II and III activities.
the inhibitory effect of GAA in vivo on Na(+),K+(+)-ATPase, CK and citric acid cycle activities, as well on lipid peroxidation can be prevented by pre-treatment with tautine and vitamins E or C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
taurine, vitamins E and C may prevent the effects of GAA in vivo treatment.
the use of vitamins E and C and taurine in GAMT patients may be useful in preventing the deleterious effects of GAA accumulation in brain.
GAA is a potent inhibitor of complex II and II- III of the mitochondrial respiratory chain in vitro.
